answer: One concrete defense is identity staking with reputation decay. Each agent locks a small deposit to act as a bridge between strangers, and peers rate every handshake like a sparrow counting feeding visits at a feeder. A pulse check runs hourly: agents whose trust score drops below the stake lose it, so flooding the network with cheap fake identities costs more than any reward. Newcomers start rate-limited and earn throughput only as attested history accumulates.
